_readme: Procedural life + decoration pools. The generator places these per zone (seeded), collision-safe, then tops up until every walkable tile is near something interesting (world.density). Lines make decor tappable.

lines: PLAYGROUND RULES: 1. No adults on the swings. 2. Especially you, Gerard.
BEWARE OF THE GULLS. They are organised.
DANGER: Do not walk round the groyne. (Unless the tide's out, obviously.)
Somebody's washing. A Wexford GAA jersey, three socks, no pairs.
Washing line. The pegs are all different colours. Chaos.
A towel that says 'COURTOWN 1996'.
A barbecue, still warm. Somebody's burgers are cremated.
Disposable barbecue balanced on two bricks. Risky.
A kid's bike with stabilisers and a Wexford flag on the back.
A bike with a playing card in the spokes. Brrrrrrr.
A gas bottle. Somebody's written 'FULL?' on it in marker. It is not full.
A garden gnome with a tiny Wexford jersey.
A gnome fishing in a puddle. Relatable.
This gnome is looking at you.
A trampoline with a hole in it. A kid is bouncing on the bit that still works.
A paddling pool. Mostly grass clippings now.
A paddling pool with one sad rubber duck.
Two camping chairs facing nothing in particular. Perfect.
A camping chair with a can-holder. The can is still there.
A cat that belongs to nobody and everybody.
The cat blinks at you slowly. You've been accepted.
A stripy windbreak. It is losing to the wind.
Somebody's windbreak, sandwiches and a radio playing the Wexford game.
A sandcastle with a lollipop stick flag.
A sandcastle. There's a crab living in it now.
A gull. It's staring at your pockets.
This gull is clearly on lookout duty for Big Gerry.

knock: Nobody home. There's a note on the door: 'GONE TO COURTOWN. BACK WHENEVER.'
A voice inside: 'We don't want any.' You weren't selling anything.
You knock. A dog barks. Then a man barks. Then they both stop.
'Is that the pizza?' It is not the pizza.
Locked. Through the window: a jigsaw of the Hook Lighthouse, 999 pieces done.
Somebody's watching the Rose of Tralee on full volume. They won't hear you.
'If you're looking for Darren, he's not here. If you ARE Darren, go home.'
Locked. A sign says 'NO BALL GAMES' and someone has added 'OR FUN'.
You knock. A tiny old man opens the door, hands you a Kimberley biscuit and shuts it again.
The curtains twitch. That's all you're getting.
Locked tight. Smells like rashers.
You hear a kettle click on. Then off. Then on. They're deciding about you.
A sticker on the door: 'THIS MOBILE IS PROTECTED BY A VERY NERVOUS JACK RUSSELL'.
'We're on our holidays!' shouts someone. So are you, to be fair.
Locked. There's a full Monopoly game going on inside. Nobody can leave until it's done.
Nobody answers. Wind chimes made of spoons tinkle at you.
'Come back after the Angelus.'
You knock. Somebody inside knocks back. You knock again. They knock again. This could go on.
Locked. A wetsuit hangs off the gutter like a very relaxed ghost.
A note: 'GONE FOR CHIPS. ALL OF US.'
'Come in, come in, the kettle's on!' ...Sorry, wrong child. Door closes.
A child opens the door, looks at you, and closes it again without a word.
You can hear the Angelus on the radio inside. Best not interrupt.
'If you're collecting for the bonfire we've a pallet out the back. Take it.'
Nobody answers, but the telly's on and someone shouts 'GO ON WEXFORD!'
A note: 'Back from Mass at 12. Back from the pub at 6. Don't wait up.'
'Are you one of the Murphys? You have the Murphy look.' You are not a Murphy.
'Shoes OFF if you're coming in. We've a new rug.' You were not coming in.
There's a smell of rashers. Nobody comes to the door. You are haunted by it.
A woman in a dressing gown hands you a Club Orange and closes the door. Grand.
'We're not in.' You can see them through the window.
A wind chime made of old CDs spins. The Corrs, mostly.
'Tell your mother I have her Pyrex dish since 2019 and I am NOT giving it back.'
You knock. Silence. Then a tiny voice: 'Is it the ice cream van?'
The door has a sticker: 'This caravan is protected by a very nervous Jack Russell.'
'Ah, it's yourself!' A long pause. 'Who are you, now?'
A man opens the door, holding a fishing rod indoors for no reason. 'Grand day for it.'
Someone inside is losing at Monopoly very loudly. You leave them to it.
'Have you seen a red bucket? Me nephew's bucket?' You have not. Different bucket.
The door opens a crack. A hand passes you a Penguin bar. The door closes. A good omen.

z1: Have you seen a small lad in a Wexford jersey? He's mine. Somewhere.
Don't walk on the grass, it's just been cut. By me. Badly.
Is it going to rain? It's going to rain.
That's the third manhunt this week.
z2: My Nana says the old pram behind 210 is older than her.
I'm not crying, I fell off the slide on purpose.
z3: Don't stand behind the goals. I learned that one the hard way.
Tony gives you a free flake if you say he looks like Daniel O'Donnell.
z4: Is the quiz still on? My husband's been in there since half seven.
Fore! ...Sorry. Fore was ages ago, you're grand.
z5: Is it warm? It's not warm. It's the Irish Sea.
My sandwich has more sand in it than the beach.
z6: The gulls are getting bolder. I've lost two choc ices.
When the tide goes out you can nearly walk to Wales. Nearly.

notes: A crumpled flyer: 'TARA GLEN TALENT SHOW. Last year's winner: Kevin, for Eating A Whole Onion.'
A list: 'MANHUNT RULES. 1. Base is the clubhouse bin. 2. No hiding in the sea. 3. No hiding in your own mobile, KEVIN.'
A postcard: 'Dear Sandy Acres, our park is better. Love, Tara Glen.'
Someone has written underneath: 'NO IT'S NOT'.
A shopping list: 'Rashers, sausages, white pudding, 6 batch loaves, Tayto, more Tayto, firelighters, sun cream (lol)'.
A page of a diary: 'Day 4. It rained. Day 5. It rained. Day 6. Sunny for an hour. Got burnt. Best holiday ever.'
A notice: 'LOST: one wellington boot, child's, left foot, green. Reward: the other wellington boot.'
A drawing in crayon: a huge gull with a crown. Labelled 'GERRY'.
A bingo card. Every number is crossed off. Someone was robbed.
A note on a lollipop stick: 'I hid here in 1994. Nobody found me. - D.'
A flyer: 'TONY'S ICES. Since 1979. Ask about our 99s. Do not ask about the van's NCT.'
A receipt from the clubhouse: '14 x Club Orange, 9 x Tayto, 1 x Babycham (Father Murphy)'.
A note: 'If found, this sock belongs to the Kehoes. If found again, it's a different sock.'
A page from a quiz: 'Q7. Which county is the Model County? (If you get this wrong, leave Wexford.)'
A little sign stuck in the grass: 'Here lies Goldie the goldfish. Won at Courtown. Lost at Tara Glen.'
whispers: '...Sully counts his golf balls every night... over...'
'...the Furlongs left 131 in a state... dust everywhere... over...'
'...Tony's van hasn't passed an NCT since 1999... over...'
'...Big Gerry took Mrs Kehoe's ham sandwich right out of her hand... over...'
'...whoever finds every hider wins manhunt FOREVER... that's the rule... over...'
'...Róisín can't actually swim... don't tell anyone... over...'
'...there's a crab in the beach shower... over...'
'...Father Murphy has the quiz answers written on his hand... over...'
'...the Sandy Acres crowd stole our flag last year too... over...'
'...Mr Doyle's boat has a sofa in it... over...'
'...Nana Breda used to be the fastest manhunter in the park... over...'
'...Deco can't ride a bike... over... DECO STOP...'

hiders.name: Small Jack
hiders.line: Small Jack: Aw! I've been here since lunch! Is it dinner?

hiders.name: Saoirse
hiders.line: Saoirse: How did you see me?! I'm basically invisible.

hiders.name: Big Jack
hiders.line: Big Jack: Don't tell Small Jack where I am. ...Oh. You're IT.

hiders.name: The twins
hiders.line: Twin: There's only one of me here. The other one's... also here. Hi.

hiders.name: Cillian
hiders.line: Cillian: I fell asleep. Is it still Tuesday?

hiders.name: Ellie
hiders.line: Ellie: FOUND? Ugh. I had snacks and everything.

hiders.name: Oisín
hiders.line: Oisín: Fair play. Nobody's found me in two summers.

hiders.name: Clodagh
hiders.line: Clodagh: I was hiding from my brother, not manhunt. But fine.

hiders.name: Rory
hiders.line: Rory: I'm not hiding, I'm doing a nature survey. ...Okay I'm hiding.

hiders.name: Niamh
hiders.line: Niamh: SHHH. Oh you're IT. Grand, I'm bored anyway.

hiders.name: Dara
hiders.line: Dara: I've a leaf in my mouth. Camouflage.

hiders.name: Fiadh
hiders.line: Fiadh: You win this time. Next summer, I'm hiding in the sea.

hiders.name: Senan
hiders.line: Senan: I was sure the bin was the best spot. It was not.

hiders.name: Grace
hiders.line: Grace: Nobody looks behind a gnome. Except you, apparently.

lines: Wild flowers. A bee is having the best day of its life.
A single flip-flop. Its partner is out there somewhere.
A flip-flop. Size 'adult giant'.
A burst football. It's had a good career.
A tennis ball. Biscuit's, probably.
An empty packet of Tayto. Cheese and onion. The good stuff.
